title: Orsen and the Mixtape
premise: Orsen Vale has one shot at a music scholarship, and his final audition falls in three weeks. When his best friend Lena Brightwater — the girl who raised her younger siblings while their mother worked nights and who never let anyone past her locked locker — vanishes without a trace, all she leaves behind is a keyring and an unlabeled mixtape hidden in his band room cubby. Following the tape's songs like a map through her double life, Orsen discovers she wasn't just surviving; she was secretly auditioning for the same scholarship, and someone connected to the program made her disappear to protect a secret. To find her, Orsen must expose what he knows — burning his own audition chances and risking the truth of how much he loved her — before the final audition becomes both her rescue and his reckoning.
about_author: Vesper Montrose is the pen name of a former night-shift radio host who grew up translating adult worries into teenage notebooks. They write stories about kids who carry too much and love anyway.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Establishes Orsen's careful, invisible routine at Halloway High and his one bright spot: lunchtime jam sessions with Lena Brightwater, who guards her home life like a vault. The emotional beat is quiet longing — he knows everything about her taste in music and nothing about her life.

chapters.title: The Empty Desk
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Lena misses three days of school. Her younger siblings, twins Sam and Junie, linger outside the band room looking lost. When Orsen checks her locker combination one last time, it's been cleaned out except for a single envelope with his name on it containing her house key and a bus token.

chapters.title: Keys That Don't Fit
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen visits Lena's apartment and meets the twins, who insist their sister 'went to get something back.' He finds a second key on her ring that matches nothing in the building. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into resolve as he realizes no adult is looking hard enough.

chapters.title: Side A
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. In his band room cubby he discovers an unlabeled cassette — Side A full of songs he and Lena used to riff on, but each track has a date and location scrawled on the insert. The first location is the closed-down Riverside record shop. Beat: the mixtape becomes a map, and fear becomes purpose.

chapters.title: The Record Shop Ghost
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins with flashbacks from Lena's journal pages tucked in the cassette case. At Riverside, Orsen learns Lena had been sneaking there for months, practicing piano after hours. The owner mentions a man in a Halloway Music Department jacket who came asking about her. Beat: the danger has a face.

chapters.title: Mr. Calloway's Office
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen probes the beloved head of the music department, Mr. Calloway, who deflects smoothly and warns him to focus on his own audition. Orsen notices the scholarship shortlist posted on the wall — two names: his, and one redacted. Beat: paranoia takes root in a place that felt safe.

chapters.title: What the Twins Know
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, with Sam and Junie's voices carrying the scene. The twins reveal Mom's night shifts stopped paying, that Lena had been working somewhere 'with microphones,' and that she cried once over a letter with a school seal. Beat: Orsen sees the price of survival Lena paid invisibly for years.

chapters.title: Side B, Track One
chapters.summary: Lena's flashback POV. Three months earlier: Lena records the first confession track — she qualified for the same scholarship Orsen is chasing but hid it, because winning would mean leaving the twins. Beat: love against duty, stated in her own voice for the first time.

chapters.title: The Practice Room Tapes
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Following Track Two's coordinates to the school's basement practice rooms, Orsen finds evidence someone searched them recently — and a torn corner of the redacted shortlist naming L. BRIGHTWATER. Beat: confirmation that Lena was erased deliberately, not accidentally.

chapters.title: An Accomplice Named Dev
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen finally trusts someone: Dev, his rival-turned-friend in jazz band, who admits Calloway asked students to report 'unauthorized practice hours.' Dev saw Lena escorted out by a man claiming to be her uncle. Beat: the cost of trust — and its first dividend.

chapters.title: The Uncle Lie
chapters.summary: Lena's flashback POV. Lena is confronted by Grant Ellery, a program booster and Calloway's old friend, who offers to make her scholarship problem disappear if she withdraws quietly. She refuses. Beat: her spine established; the trap closing.

chapters.title: Missing Persons, Minimal Effort
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Police interview the twins perfunctorily and close the file within days — no guardian will press, and Lena is 'almost eighteen.' Orsen rages at a system built to look past kids like her. Beat: righteous anger; the stakes become systemic, not personal.

chapters.title: Track Five Is a Confession
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. On the tape, Lena finally speaks directly to Orsen: she tells him she loves the sessions they had, that she never said so because wanting things got people hurt. Beat: heartbreak — the friendship's unspoken truth arrives only after she's gone.

chapters.title: Breaking Into the Booster Files
chapters.summary: Orsen and Dev's POV, split. The pair infiltrate the boosters' storage during the winter recital, finding withdrawal letters forged in Lena's handwriting and a ledger of 'adjusted' scholarships stretching back years. Beat: triumph shadowed by dread — this is bigger than one girl.

chapters.title: Calloway's Choice
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen confronts Calloway privately. Calloway confesses he looked away years ago to keep his own program funded, and reveals Ellery keeps noncompliant students 'somewhere they can think' — a family property upstate. Beat: a mentor's fall; a thread of hope.

chapters.title: The Audition Letter
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen receives official notice: his final audition is moved up to Saturday — the same day he plans to drive upstate. Ellery is sending a message. Beat: duty versus love made literal; Orsen must choose which future to sacrifice.

chapters.title: Side B, Last Track
chapters.summary: Lena's present-day POV. Held at the Ellery property, Lena records one last message on a salvaged recorder, addressed to whoever finds the first tape: don't come for me, finish the audition, live loudly enough for both of us. Beat: self-sacrifice as love letter.

chapters.title: Two Roads Out of Town
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Saturday morning. Orsen stands in the audition hallway holding his guitar case, then walks out mid-sign-in, Dev covering for him with a lie that could get Dev expelled too. Beat: the point of no return, chosen freely.

chapters.title: The House Where Songs Go to Wait
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. At the property, Orsen plays Side B loud from the driveway until a window lights. He finds Lena thin and furious and alive; Ellery arrives, and Orsen livestreams the confrontation and the forged letters to the boosters' own mailing list. Beat: climax — truth as weapon.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Ellery is arrested; Calloway resigns rather than name names; the district voids the tampered scholarships. Orsen faces the principal and tells the whole truth, including his own walkout, accepting whatever comes. Beat: consequences owned, not dodged.

chapters.title: The Second Audition
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Weeks later, an independent panel grants both Orsen and Lena a reopened audition slot. Lena performs a song she wrote in captivity; Orsen accompanies her without being asked. Beat: love against duty resolved — they stop choosing between futures and build one together.

chapters.title: Coda: Recorded Live
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Spring. The twins eat dinner at a table with money actually in the bank; the mixtape gets a proper label: FOR ORSEN, SIDE C TO COME. Orsen and Lena book a gig at the old record shop. Final beat: survival was the beginning, not the story — the story is what they play next.
